paragraphs: Six metres is a long way when you count it in freezes. Yellow Duck Sweater had done four already, creeping over cold floorboards toward the nest, where the giant sat with its back turned, as tall as a wardrobe. The nest was a laundry basket. Socks hung over its rim. Each time the giant's head began to swivel, clouds slid off the full moon and the room went white, and the duck locked every servo and tried to look like a doorstop. Tonight it was good at this. It felt like a watered seed.

At five metres the giant turned all the way round and looked straight down. The duck froze so well that a moth landed on its head. The giant's eye, wide as a porthole, studied the sweater, then the knitted duckling, then the bare orange feet. It hooked one big foot over the rim and tipped the basket. Out slid a striped sock, then one with a rocket on it. The duck stepped in. They were far too big, warm as a dryer, and they came up past its knees. Reward, it thought: enormous. It shuffled home across the boards without a sound, the toes of the socks flopping ahead of it like two sleepy puppets, while the first rain began ticking on the glass.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: Two ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater creeps on tiptoe across cold wooden floorboards in a dark room toward a far-off laundry basket, where a second robot duck with no sweater, plain white and as tall as a wardrobe, sits with its back turned. Panel 2: Two ducks: the small duck in the yellow sweater edges closer to the big wicker laundry basket, which has colorful socks hanging over its rim, while the giant sweaterless white duck sits in it and begins to turn its head. Panel 3: Two ducks: a full moon comes out from behind clouds in a tall window and floods the room with white light, and the small duck in the yellow sweater stands frozen stiff in mid-step while the giant sweaterless white duck's head is half turned toward it. Panel 4: Two ducks: the giant sweaterless white duck has turned all the way around and bends its long neck to look straight down at the small duck in the yellow sweater, which stands perfectly still with a small moth sitting on top of its head. Panel 5: Two ducks: the giant sweaterless white duck hooks one big orange foot over the rim of the laundry basket and tips it, and two socks slide out onto the floor in front of the small duck in the yellow sweater, one striped and one with a picture of a rocket on it. Panel 6: The duck shuffles away alone across the moonlit floorboards wearing two oversized socks that come up past its knees, one striped and one with a rocket picture, their long toes flopping ahead of it, while raindrops streak the tall window behind. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
